editorial.headline: Processed-Food Retail Has a Clear National Opening—and a Bali Stop
editorial.standfirst: This specialist food-retail activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet PMA registration in Bali is blocked under the province’s permanent risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
**A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today.** That blunt conclusion matters because, at national level, the activity is open to foreign investment. The business itself is specialised retail trade in food commodities produced by industry. Its stated examples give the category a clear shape: pickled fruit and vegetables, preserved fruit and vegetables, crackers, and emping or ceriping. The focus is the retail sale of these food products—not a generic description of food commerce, but a defined lane for industrially produced foods of this kind.

The natural registrant is therefore a retail operator whose offering centres on these specified food commodities. The record makes the activity available across the full stated range of business scales: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That breadth is useful context, but it does not dilute the underlying character of the activity. Its commercial identity remains specialised retailing of the listed types of processed food products, with the examples serving as the practical guide to what belongs within the scope.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain English, the national framework permits full foreign ownership for this activity. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. For a founder assessing the national position alone, this is an activity with a fully open foreign-investment ceiling and availability across the listed business scales.

Bali changes the result entirely. The Bali status is Blocked (risk class): blocked by risk class. The record states that the OSS risk assessment at the Besar scale is Low or Medium-Low across every scope, placing the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent block on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. The stated moratorium took effect in May 2026. Accordingly, the national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling does not create a Bali registration route for a foreign investor. The national position remains open; the Bali position is a present block on PMA registration.
editorial.pullQuote: A 100% national foreign-ownership ceiling does not change the fact that this activity is blocked for PMA registration in Bali today.
